exposure: mode of delivery (LSCS vs. normal vaginal delivery)
outcome: newborn complications (respiratory distress syndrome, septicemia, intraventricular hemorrhage)
cohort: The study participants were pregnant women at term pregnancy (37-42 wks) presenting with premature rupture of membranes, admitted in the labour room of SHKBMC of Jhalawar Medical College, Jhalawar.
finding: Maternal morbidity and neonatal morbidity were associated with premature rupture of membranes (PROM).
mod_finding: 42.50% of cases delivered by LSCS and 57.50% were delivered by normal vaginal delivery.
birth_weight: Babies had birth weights categorized as between 2-2.5 kg (49.38%), >2.5 kg (33.75%), and <2.0 kg (16.88%).
